title: Natural English at Work
description: Sound natural in professional and academic situations with verb + noun collocations (make, do, take, have), phrasal verbs for work and study, adjective + preposition combinations, and common business collocations.
objectives: Choose correctly between make, do, take and have in common collocations
Use phrasal verbs for work and study accurately, including word order with pronouns
Use adjectives with the correct dependent prepositions
Use business and career collocations in meetings, emails and interviews

lessons.title: Collocations with Make and Do
lessons.summary: Membedakan kolokasi dengan make dan do.
objectives: Understand the general difference between make (create/produce) and do (activities/tasks)
Learn the most common fixed collocations with make and do
Avoid typical errors such as do a mistake and make homework
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Why collocations matter
A **collocation** is a combination of words that native speakers naturally use together. *Make a mistake* sounds natural; *do a mistake* sounds wrong, even though the meaning is clear. Collocations are one of the main differences between B1 and B2 English.

### The general rule
| make | do |
| --- | --- |
| create, produce, build something new | perform an activity, task or job |
| *make a cake, make a plan, make a film* | *do the housework, do your homework, do a course* |

But many collocations are simply **fixed** and must be learned.

### Common collocations with make
| Category | Collocations |
| --- | --- |
| communication | make a **phone call**, make a **complaint**, make a **suggestion**, make a **comment**, make an **excuse**, make a **promise** |
| decisions & plans | make a **decision**, make **plans**, make an **arrangement**, make an **appointment** |
| results | make **progress**, make a **profit/loss**, make **money**, make a **difference**, make a **mistake** |
| effort | make an **effort**, make **sure** |
| others | make **friends**, make **room/space**, make the **bed** |

### Common collocations with do
| Category | Collocations |
| --- | --- |
| work & study | do **homework**, do **research**, do a **course**, do an **exam** (BrE), do **business** |
| housework | do the **shopping**, do the **washing-up**, do the **cleaning**, do the **laundry** |
| general | do **your best**, do **someone a favour**, do **harm/good**, do **damage**, do **well/badly** |
| *-ing* activities | do **some reading/writing/exercise** |

### Tricky pairs
| ✓ | ✗ |
| --- | --- |
| make a mistake | do a mistake |
| do homework | make homework |
| make progress | do progress |
| do research | make research |
| do someone a favour | make someone a favour |
| make an effort | do an effort |

### Learning tip
Record collocations as chunks in sentences, not single words: *We've made a lot of progress, but we still need to do more research.*

> **Catatan:** Bahasa Indonesia memakai *membuat* dan *melakukan* dengan cara yang berbeda, jadi jangan menerjemahkan langsung. *Membuat kesalahan* = **make** a mistake (cocok), tetapi *mengerjakan PR* = **do** homework, dan *melakukan penelitian* = **do** research. Hafalkan sebagai paket.

lessons.title: Collocations with Take and Have
lessons.summary: Kolokasi umum dengan take dan have dalam konteks kerja dan belajar.
objectives: Use common collocations with take (take part in, take place, take into account)
Use common collocations with have (have a look, have a word with, have difficulty)
Avoid errors such as make a photo and do part in
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Collocations with take
| Collocation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| take a break | rest for a short time | Let's **take a** ten-minute **break**. |
| take a photo | photograph | Can you **take a photo** of us? |
| take part (in) | participate | Twenty teams **took part in** the competition. |
| take place | happen (planned events) | The conference **takes place** in March. |
| take notes | write notes | Please **take notes** during the meeting. |
| take responsibility (for) | accept that you are responsible | She **took responsibility for** the error. |
| take advantage of | use an opportunity | **Take advantage of** the free training. |
| take something into account | consider | We must **take the cost into account**. |
| take a risk / a chance | do something risky | He **took a risk** and started a company. |

### Collocations with have
| Collocation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| have a look (at) | look | Can I **have a look at** your notes? |
| have a go / a try | try | **Have a go** — it's easy! |
| have a word (with sb) | speak briefly, often privately | Could I **have a word with** you? |
| have a chat | talk informally | We **had a** quick **chat** after the meeting. |
| have a meeting | meet formally | We're **having a meeting** at 3. |
| have an argument | argue | They **had an argument** about money. |
| have difficulty / trouble (in) + -ing | find it hard | I'm **having difficulty understanding** the software. |

### take a break or have a break?
Both are correct. *Have a break* is slightly more British; *take a break* is common everywhere.

### Watch the grammar
- *take place* is **intransitive** and never passive: ✗ *The meeting was taken place.*
- *have difficulty* + **-ing** (not *to*): ✗ *I have difficulty to understand.*
- *take part* **in** (not *at* or *on*).
- *take into account*: with a short object, put it in the middle: *take **the cost** into account*.

> **Catatan:** *Ambil foto* = **take** a photo (bukan *make a photo*). *Ikut serta* = **take part in**. *Berlangsung* (acara) = **take place**. *Saya kesulitan memahami ...* = **I'm having difficulty understanding ...** (pakai -ing).

lessons.title: Phrasal Verbs for Work and Study
lessons.summary: Phrasal verb yang sering dipakai di tempat kerja dan dunia akademik, termasuk urutan kata dengan pronoun.
objectives: Use common phrasal verbs for work and study (carry out, set up, take on, put off, hand in)
Distinguish separable and inseparable phrasal verbs
Place object pronouns correctly (put it off, not put off it)
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Key phrasal verbs
| Phrasal verb | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| carry out | do (research, a survey, a task) | We **carried out** a survey of 500 customers. |
| set up | start (a company, a meeting) | She **set up** her own business in 2022. |
| take on | employ; accept work | We're **taking on** three new staff. / Don't **take on** too much. |
| put off | postpone | The meeting has been **put off** until Friday. |
| hand in | submit (work) | Please **hand in** your essays by Monday. |
| come up with | think of (an idea) | He **came up with** a brilliant solution. |
| look into | investigate | We'll **look into** your complaint. |
| deal with | handle | Who's **dealing with** this client? |
| run out of | have none left | We've **run out of** paper. |
| catch up on | do things you didn't have time for | I need to **catch up on** my emails. |
| follow up (on) | take further action | I'll **follow up on** our conversation. |
| fill in | complete (a form) | **Fill in** the application form. |

### Separable or inseparable?
**Separable** phrasal verbs (verb + particle) can have the object in the middle or at the end:
- *Hand **your essays** in.* / *Hand in **your essays**.*
- With a **pronoun**, the object MUST go in the middle: *Hand **them** in.* (✗ *Hand in them.*)
- Examples: *carry out, set up, put off, hand in, fill in, take on*.

**Inseparable** phrasal verbs keep the verb and particle together:
- *Look **into** it.* (✗ *Look it into.*)
- *Deal **with** them.* / *Come up **with** an idea.* / *Run out **of** time.*
- Three-part phrasal verbs (*come up with, run out of, catch up on*) are always inseparable.

### Formal alternatives
In formal writing, you can often use a one-word verb: *carry out → conduct*, *put off → postpone*, *look into → investigate*, *set up → establish*, *hand in → submit*. Both are correct; choose according to style.

> **Catatan:** Phrasal verb sulit karena maknanya tidak bisa ditebak dari kata per kata. *Put off* = menunda (bukan 'menaruh mati'). Ingat aturan pronoun: **put it off** ✓, **put off it** ✗. Untuk tulisan formal, gunakan padanan satu kata (*postpone, submit, investigate*).

sections.summary: Key phrasal verbs: **carry out, set up, take on, put off, hand in, come up with, look into, deal with, run out of, catch up on, follow up, fill in**. With separable verbs, pronouns go in the middle (*put it off*); inseparable verbs never split (*look into it*). *Ringkasan: put it off ✓, put off it ✗.*

lessons.title: Adjective + Preposition
lessons.summary: Kata sifat yang diikuti preposisi tertentu (good at, responsible for, aware of, familiar with).
objectives: Use common adjective + preposition combinations for work and study
Describe your skills and experience accurately in applications and interviews
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Dependent prepositions
Many adjectives are followed by a **fixed preposition**. The choice is not logical, so learn them in groups.

| Preposition | Adjectives | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **at** | good, bad, skilled, brilliant, hopeless | She's **good at** solving problems. |
| **in** | interested, involved, experienced, skilled | I'm **experienced in** project management. |
| **of** | aware, capable, proud, afraid, fond, tired | He's **capable of** working under pressure. |
| **for** | responsible, famous, eligible, suitable, grateful | She's **responsible for** the budget. |
| **with** | familiar, satisfied, pleased, bored, fed up | Are you **familiar with** this software? |
| **on** | keen, dependent, based | I'm **keen on** learning new skills. |
| **to** | used, committed, similar, accustomed | I'm **used to** working late. |
| **about** | worried, excited, enthusiastic, concerned | We're **excited about** the launch. |

### Preposition + -ing
After all these prepositions, use a **noun** or the **-ing form**:
- ✓ *I'm interested **in applying** for the position.*
- ✗ *I'm interested to apply...* (possible in some contexts, but *in applying* is the standard pattern for job applications)
- ✓ *I'm used **to working** late.* (*to* is a preposition here!)

### Same adjective, different preposition
| Combination | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| good **at** (a skill) | *good at maths* |
| good **for** (benefit) | *Exercise is good for you.* |
| good **with** (people/tools) | *good with children / good with numbers* |
| responsible **for** (a task) | *responsible for training* |
| responsible **to** (a person) | *responsible to the director* |

### Useful for job applications
*I am **experienced in** customer service, **familiar with** most design programs and **keen on** developing my leadership skills. I am also **capable of** working independently.*

> **Catatan:** Preposisi setelah kata sifat sering berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia: *tertarik **pada*** = interested **in**; *bertanggung jawab **atas*** = responsible **for**; *puas **dengan*** = satisfied **with** (sama), *sadar **akan*** = aware **of**. Setelah preposisi selalu pakai **-ing**.

lessons.title: Business and Career Collocations
lessons.summary: Kolokasi bisnis dan karier untuk rapat, email, dan wawancara kerja.
objectives: Use business collocations (meet a target, launch a product, strike a deal, chair a meeting)
Use career collocations (apply for a position, gain experience, climb the career ladder)
Sound natural and polite in meetings and interviews
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the speaking task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas berbicara dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Business collocations
| Collocation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| meet / miss a target | reach / not reach a goal | We **met our sales target** in June. |
| launch a product | introduce it to the market | They **launched** a new app last month. |
| run a business | manage a business | She **runs** a small catering **business**. |
| strike / close a deal | reach a business agreement | We **struck a deal** with a supplier. |
| chair / hold a meeting | lead / organise a meeting | Who's **chairing** the **meeting**? |
| raise an issue | mention a problem for discussion | I'd like to **raise** an **issue**. |
| reach / make a decision | decide | We need to **reach a decision** today. |
| draw up a contract / plan | prepare a document | The lawyer **drew up** the **contract**. |
| cut costs | reduce spending | The firm had to **cut costs**. |

### Career collocations
| Collocation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| apply **for** a job / position | ask formally for a job |
| gain / get experience | get experience |
| climb the career ladder | get promoted step by step |
| be offered / turn down a job | receive / refuse a job offer |
| hand in your notice | tell your employer you are leaving |
| work flexible hours / work remotely | (see Unit 1) |

### Natural meeting language
| Function | Natural phrases |
| --- | --- |
| opening | *Shall we get started? / The main aim of today's meeting is...* |
| raising an issue | *I'd like to raise the issue of... / Can I bring up something?* |
| agreeing | *I'm with you on that. / That makes sense.* |
| disagreeing politely | *I see your point, but... / I'm not sure that's the best option.* |
| concluding | *So, to sum up, we've agreed to... / Let's follow up on this next week.* |

### Interview language
*I have **gained** a lot of **experience** in customer service. I'm **responsible for** a team of five. I'm **keen on taking on** new challenges, and I'd like to **climb the career ladder** in a company like yours.*

### raise vs rise
**raise** (transitive: raise *something*): *raise an issue, raise prices*. **rise** (intransitive): *Prices rose.* ✗ *rise an issue*.

> **Catatan:** Kolokasi bisnis membuat bahasa Inggris Anda terdengar profesional. *Mencapai target* = **meet** a target (bukan *reach* — walaupun *reach a target* juga dipakai, *meet a target* paling umum). *Mengajukan masalah* = **raise** an issue. *Melamar pekerjaan* = **apply for** a job.

questions.explanation: The collocation is **meet a target** (mencapai target).

questions.prompt: Match each verb with the noun it collocates with.
questions.explanation: **chair a meeting, launch a product, strike a deal, draw up a contract, gain experience**.

questions.prompt: Job interview: answer the question "Tell me about your experience and why you're interested in this position." Speak for about one minute and use at least five collocations from this unit.
questions.sampleAnswer: I've gained five years of experience in customer service, and for the last two years I've been responsible for a team of six people. We've met our targets every quarter, and last year I came up with a new system for dealing with complaints that cut response times by half. I'm keen on taking on new challenges, which is why I'm applying for this position. I'm familiar with your products, and I'd like to climb the career ladder in a company that values innovation.
questions.explanation: A strong answer uses natural collocations, perfect tenses for experience, and adjective + preposition combinations.

dialogue.speaker: Chair
dialogue.text: Before we finish, does anyone want to raise any other issues?

options: Yes, I'd like to raise the issue of our delivery times.
Yes, I'd like to rise the issue of our delivery times.
Yes, I'd like to make up the issue of our delivery times.
Yes, I'd like to take the issue our delivery times.
questions.explanation: **raise the issue of + noun** is the natural collocation. *Rise* has no object, and the other options are not natural.

questions.sentence: We need to do a decision about the budget by Friday.
answers: We need to make a decision about the budget by Friday.
We need to reach a decision about the budget by Friday.
We need to come to a decision about the budget by Friday.
We need to take a decision about the budget by Friday.
questions.explanation: We **make** (or *reach / come to / take*) a decision, never *do* a decision.

questions.prompt: Complete the text with words from the bank.
questions.text: After five years in sales, Lina decided to ___ for a management position. She had ___ a lot of experience, and the company was planning to ___ a new branch in Makassar.
questions.explanation: **apply for** a position; **gain experience**; **open a branch**.

unitTestQuestions.context: I'll ___ some research on our competitors before the meeting.

unitTestQuestions.text: The survey was carried ___ by a team of university students.

unitTestQuestions.explanation: **capable of + -ing**: *She is very capable of managing a large team.*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Match each noun with the verb it collocates with.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **make a complaint, do the washing-up, take a photo, have a chat**.

unitTestQuestions.text: Can we ___ the meeting until Thursday? I'm not ___ with the new figures yet.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **put off** = postpone; **familiar with** = know well. (*aware of*, *keen on*)

unitTestQuestions.source: Kami harus mengambil keputusan hari ini.
answers: We have to make a decision today.
We must make a decision today.
We need to make a decision today.
We have to take a decision today.
We must take a decision today.
We need to take a decision today.
We have to reach a decision today.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Mengambil keputusan* = **make a decision** (BrE also *take a decision*), not *do a decision*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the phrasal verb take on.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: The company employed fifty new staff last year.
answers: The company took on fifty new staff last year.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **take on** = employ (merekrut): *The company took on fifty new staff.*
